images.title: A dental office is hiring an *Administrative Coordinator*
images.sub: What an AI Employee would do in each of the six duties on the posting, and what the seat costs.

images.name: posting
images.title: Administrative Coordinator, Dental Office
duties: Fill cancellations and keep the schedule flowing
Respond to patient inquiries by phone and email
Assist with payments, insurance processing and administrative support
Support reception and front desk operations as needed
images.qualifications: Previous administrative experience required. Dental experience is an asset.
images.note: Duties condensed from a real Indeed posting. Company name and address removed.

images.name: quote
images.text: Most of this job is keeping the *hygiene chairs full* and getting an *insurance answer* before the patient sits down.

images.name: breakdown
images.title: What the AI Employee does *in each duty*
rows: Works the recall list every morning, texts patients who are due and books their pick into the hygiene column.
Messages the short-notice list the moment a slot opens and books the first patient who confirms.
Builds the estimate from the signed treatment plan, sends the predetermination and chases the insurer.
Answers routine questions at any hour and books or moves appointments. Clinical questions go to the dentist.
Submits claims, posts payments and sends balance reminders. Refunds, write-offs and payment plans wait for a person.
Sends intake forms, confirms tomorrow's patients, checks eligibility and picks up the phone when the desk is busy.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A Tuesday for the *AI Administrative Coordinator*
rows: A patient cancels a 10 am cleaning. It texts the short-notice list and books the first reply by 7:25.
Works the recall list: 14 patients due this month get a text with three open hygiene times.
Builds an estimate for a crown from the signed treatment plan and sends the predetermination to the insurer.
A patient calls about a swollen jaw. It takes the details, holds the emergency slot and passes it to the dentist.
Posts three insurance payments that came in overnight and matches each to its claim.
A patient asks for a refund on a prepaid whitening kit. It sends the request to the office manager to approve.
Confirms tomorrow's patients, checks their insurance eligibility and sends intake forms to two new patients.
Answers an email asking whether a filling is covered and books the appointment for next week.
images.source: Example day, built from the duties in the posting

images.name: setup
images.title: How it's *set up*
steps: Start from this posting, then sit with whoever runs the desk now. Appointment lengths, recall rules and every 'we always do it this way' get written down.
The practice management software, the claims network, the phone line, email, texting and the billing screen. Each gets only the permissions the job needs.
The fee guide, which insurers need a predetermination, what the office says about bills and how it talks to nervous patients.
Recalls, confirmations and cancellation fills it does alone. Estimates it does and reports. Refunds, write-offs and clinical questions go to a person.
For the first stretch it drafts and a person approves. As the log shows it gets things right, it takes on more.
Someone reviews the log, fixes what it got wrong and updates it when the fee guide, insurers, staff or software change.
